c.tagline: New Zealand's sunniest city and craft-loving gateway to Abel Tasman.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis such as Nelson City Taxis and Sun City Taxis are the main option; Uber coverage is very limited, so booking a local cab by phone or app is more reliable.

emergency.note: 111 is the single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance across New Zealand; Nelson Hospital runs the region's main emergency department.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The compact heart of Nelson around Trafalgar Street and the hilltop Christ Church Cathedral, packed with cafes, galleries, boutiques and the Saturday market; the most walkable base for first-timers.
A leafy heritage neighbourhood of restored villas just north of the centre, within walking distance of town yet quiet and residential; suits travellers wanting character and calm.
Nelson's main beach suburb on a long golden sweep of sand with a holiday park, playground and cafes; a relaxed, family-friendly base a short drive or bus ride from town.
The waterfront strip along Wakefield Quay and Port Nelson, lined with seafood restaurants and bars looking over the harbour and Tasman Bay; best for dining and sunset views.
A larger suburban area between Nelson and Richmond with shopping, Founders Heritage Park nearby and easy access to wineries; a practical, budget-friendly base with more space.
lodging: The Honest Lawyer, an Ascend Collection Hotel

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: NBus services run roughly 7am to 7pm on weekdays with limited Saturday services and little or no Sunday or evening service; taxis fill the gaps outside those hours.
transit.note: Nelson's public transport is the small NBus network run by Nelson City Council; there is no rail, and the flat, compact centre is easily walked or cycled.
transit.pay: Tap on and off with a prepaid Bee Card for the cheapest fare, or pay the driver with cash; the network is limited, so many visitors rely on walking, cycling or taxis.

bus: InterCity coaches to Picton, Blenheim, Christchurch and the West Coast
Abel Tasman shuttle services to Motueka, Kaiteriteri and Marahau
ferry: Abel Tasman water taxis from Kaiteriteri and Marahau (seasonal, ~1 hr drive from the city)

transit.m: Super Shuttle door-to-door shared van to the city (~15 min)
Airport taxi to central Nelson (~10 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in New Zealand; rounding up or leaving ~10% for exceptional service is appreciated but never expected.

food.name: Greenshell Mussels
food.desc: New Zealand's big green-lipped mussels, farmed in the Marlborough Sounds and Tasman Bay, steamed with wine and garlic or smoked over manuka.

places.name: The Boat Shed Cafe
places.note: Nelson's landmark restaurant on stilts over the water, seasonal seafood with harbour views.

places.name: The Mussel Inn
places.note: Legendary bush pub over the hill, famous for steamed mussels and its own home brews.

places.name: The Smokehouse
places.note: Manuka-smokes local seafood on the wharf; mussels, fish and chowder to eat outside.

food.name: Nelson Bay Scallops
food.desc: Sweet Tasman Bay scallops seared hard and served on the half shell or with black pudding and cauliflower. A short, prized season.

places.name: The Apple Shed
places.note: Waterfront kitchen known for seared scallop plates with apple and horseradish.

places.name: The Boat Shed Cafe
places.note: Buys direct from local boats; scallops appear whenever the season allows.

places.name: Hopgood's and Co
places.note: Nelson's most consistently Cuisine Good Food Guide-listed restaurant, strong on local seafood.

food.name: Smoked Fish and Blue Cod
food.desc: Manuka-smoked kahawai and salmon, plus blue cod and snapper fried in beer batter and eaten out of paper by the sea.

places.name: The Smokehouse
places.note: Working smokehouse and takeaway, the regional specialist for hot-smoked local fish.

places.name: The Boat Shed Cafe
places.note: Line-caught fish of the day cooked simply, one of Nelson's benchmark meals.

places.name: Nelson Market
places.note: Saturday market with smoked fish, seafood stalls and hot food from local producers.

food.name: Nelson Cherries, Berries and Apples
food.desc: The sunniest region in New Zealand: summer cherries, boysenberries and strawberries, autumn apples and pears, eaten fresh or as pies and real-fruit ice cream.

places.name: Nelson Market
places.note: Big Saturday growers' market, the easiest place to taste the whole region at once.

places.name: Mapua Wharf
places.note: Cluster of food producers, ice cream and cafes at the mouth of the Waimea estuary.

places.name: Nelson Farmers Market
places.note: Midweek market of orchard fruit, berries and small-batch preserves from Tasman growers.

food.name: Whitebait Fritters
food.desc: Tiny translucent whitebait bound in egg and fried into a fritter, served with lemon and white bread. A short, fiercely seasonal New Zealand ritual.

places.name: The Boat Shed Cafe
places.note: Puts whitebait on the menu in season, cooked plainly the way locals insist on.

places.name: The Mussel Inn
places.note: Country pub cooking from Golden Bay rivers, whitebait when the run is on.

places.name: The Smokehouse
places.note: Seasonal fritters alongside the smoked fish counter on the wharf.

food.name: Tasman Lamb and Seasonal Plates
food.desc: Nelson lamb, venison and free-range pork cooked with regional vegetables, olive oil and orchard fruit on short, changing menus.

places.name: Hopgood's and Co
places.note: The city's long-standing fine-dining name, a fixture in national good food guides.

places.name: Arden
places.note: Historic shopfront with a leafy courtyard and a contemporary seasonal sharing menu.

places.name: Gravity Cellars
places.note: Vineyard restaurant matching creative plates to wines made on the estate.

food.name: Nelson Craft Beer
food.desc: Nelson grows some of the world's best hops and calls itself New Zealand's craft brewing capital, from crisp pilsners to big hop-forward pale ales.

places.name: McCashin's Brewery
places.note: Brewing since the 1980s; Stoke beers, Rochdale cider, tastings, tours and a bistro.

places.name: Founders Brewery
places.note: Organic brewery and cafe set in the heritage park, easy cycle from the city centre.

places.name: The Mussel Inn
places.note: Home of Captain Cooker manuka beer, a cult New Zealand brewpub.

food.name: Nelson Wine and Cider
food.desc: Aromatic whites, chardonnay and pinot noir from the Moutere hills and Waimea plains, plus real cider pressed from local apples.

places.name: Neudorf Vineyards
places.note: One of New Zealand's most respected small wineries, known for chardonnay and pinot.

places.name: Seifried Estate
places.note: Nelson's founding family winery with a cellar door and restaurant on the Waimea plains.

places.name: McCashin's Brewery
places.note: Also makes Rochdale cider from Nelson apples, poured in the taproom.

landmarks: Christ Church Cathedral
Nelson's Art Deco-Gothic cathedral crowns the Church Hill steps above Trafalgar Street, its marble tower a beacon over the city's café heart.
Centre of New Zealand Walk (Botanical Hill)
A short zigzag climb from the Botanics ends at the famous hilltop monument with panoramic views across city, mountains and Tasman Bay.
Tahunanui Beach
A vast golden arc of safe swimming sand minutes from downtown, backed by dunes, playgrounds and unforgettable sunsets over the bay.
Abel Tasman National Park
An hour away, New Zealand's smallest national park serves up golden coves, granite headlands and turquoise water via coastal track and water taxi.
Nelson Saturday Market
The region's creative soul spills into Montgomery Square each Saturday with local art, crafts, produce and street food from sunny Nelson's makers.
Founders Heritage Park
A recreated historic village of relocated buildings, vintage railway and a craft brewery, charting Nelson's pioneering past in leafy grounds.
World of WearableArt and Classic Cars Museum
Dazzling award-winning WearableArt garments share a purpose-built museum with a gleaming collection of over a hundred classic cars.
Queens Gardens and Albion Square
An immaculate Victorian garden of ponds, roses and heritage trees beside the Suter, perfect for a riverside stroll into colonial Nelson.
The Suter Art Gallery
One of New Zealand's oldest galleries, beautifully rebuilt beside Queens Gardens, showcasing regional masters like Toss Woollaston and Jane Evans.
Cable Bay
A photogenic pebble-and-sand cove twenty minutes north, joined to the mainland by a natural boulder bank, with kayaking and headland walks.

train.note: New Zealand has no international trains, and Nelson is one of the few New Zealand regions with no railway line at all, so there is no passenger rail to or from the city.

bus.note: No international coaches. InterCity (https://www.intercity.co.nz/) links Nelson to Picton, Blenheim, Christchurch and the West Coast; regional operators run daily shuttles to Motueka, Kaiteriteri and the Abel Tasman National Park trailheads.

ferry.note: No scheduled ferries from Nelson itself; the nearest inter-island Interislander and Bluebridge crossings to Wellington leave from Picton, about two hours east. Locally, water taxis run from Kaiteriteri and Marahau into Abel Tasman National Park.

half.name: Golden Bay and Farewell Spit
half.blurb: A remote bay reached over Takaka Hill, ending in a 26-kilometer sand spit that shelters wading birds.

half.name: Mapua and Rabbit Island
half.blurb: A tidal estuary village with a wharf of food stalls, facing a pine-forested island beach across the channel.

full.name: Marlborough Wine Region (Blenheim)
full.blurb: New Zealand's largest wine region, known for Sauvignon Blanc vineyards spread across the Wairau Valley.
